steps.notes: Prompt mandates L1 normalization ('probability distribution') but frozen target is L2-normalized; L1 impl FAILS, L2 PASSES.
KLD target computed on the L2 matrix with natural log; L1 (prompt-compliant) input fails; log2 also fails.
Officially skipped (no h5 target). Static only. Generation under-specified (RNG order, choices-vs-choice, insertion-vs-replacement) -> root cause of 76.4 non-reproducibility.

Passes ONLY with the exact reference RNG recipe (p=randint FIRST, then random.choices(BASES,k=N)). Position targets 163/654 are an RNG fingerprint of the unscored 76.3. Also test-case cross-contamination (tests 4,5 use 'data').

findings.evidence: Prompt (main + step): 'make sure the PWM is l1 normalized per row after adding 1' and '...such that each row is l1 normalized (so each line becomes a probability distribution)'. Docstring: 'each row is a probability distribution'. But the h5 target rows do NOT sum to 1: target test0 row0 = [0.22373276, 0.56894413, 0.1546242, 0.7761041] (sum 1.7234); uniform test2 = 0.5 everywhere (not 0.25). These equal (raw+1)/L2norm: np.linalg.norm gives [0.2237,0.5689,0.1546,0.7761] exactly, and 26/sqrt(4*26^2)=0.5. steptest: L1 impl (per prompt) -> FAIL all 3; L2 impl -> PASS all 3. The reference used np.linalg.norm (Euclidean) instead of L1 (sum). A prompt-compliant competent solver is wrongly failed.
findings.suggested_fix: Either re-freeze the target using true L1 normalization (row/row.sum) so rows are probability distributions as the prompt states, OR change the prompt/docstring to say 'L2 (Euclidean) normalized' and drop the 'probability distribution' wording. The former is correct; KL divergence in 76.2 requires proper probability distributions.

findings.evidence: Test calls compute_kld(load_motif_from_df(data)) i.e. it consumes the solver's 76.1 output. Target test0=10.10995708567541 matches natural-log KLD computed on the L2 matrix exactly; with the prompt-compliant L1 matrix KLD=7.4987 -> FAIL. steptest: L2-upstream PASS all 3, L1-upstream FAIL all 3. So 76.2 inherits the 76.1 L2 defect: any solver that follows the 76.1 prompt (L1) also fails 76.2. Also: with rows not summing to 1, this is not a true KL divergence.
findings.suggested_fix: Fixing 76.1 (use L1) and re-freezing both 76.1 and 76.2 targets resolves this. compute_kld's own natural-log logic is fine once the input is a proper distribution.

findings.evidence: Step prompt gives D_KL(P||Q)=sum P log(P/Q) with unspecified log base. Target uses natural log (ln=10.10996 matches; uniform test2 ln=8.31777 matches). log2 (the standard 'bits' convention for sequence/relative entropy in bioinformatics) gives 14.586 / 12.0 -> FAIL. A solver choosing log2 is wrongly failed even if it correctly inferred L2 in 76.1.
findings.suggested_fix: State the log base explicitly in the prompt (e.g. 'use natural logarithm').

findings.evidence: Tests 0/1/3/4 assert scan_sequence returns a specific absolute position (163 for N=240, 654 for N=1000) where the sequence comes from generate_dna(N,data) after random.seed(42). The detected position equals the insertion location p, which is a pure RNG draw. Sweep of equally-valid generate_dna implementations: order p-first vs seq-first vs seq-p-motif gives 163 / 80,171 / 148,107; background via random.choices(BASES,k=N) vs a random.choice loop flips test1 from 654 to None. Only the exact recipe (p=random.randint(0,N-1) drawn FIRST, then seq=random.choices(BASES,k=N)) reproduces BOTH 163 and 654 (steptest joint PASS 6/6). generate_dna is step 76.3 which is OFFICIALLY SKIPPED (no target, no feedback), yet 76.4's targets are an exact RNG fingerprint of its unspecified implementation. A competent solver cannot reproduce p without guessing the reference's exact random-call sequence. (Tests 2/5 -> None are robust to any reasonable impl and pass.)
findings.suggested_fix: Make 76.4 robust to insertion location: have the test assert the detected position is within +/- (motif length) of the returned inserted_position, instead of a frozen absolute integer. Alternatively pin generate_dna's RNG protocol exactly in the 76.3 prompt and score it. As-is, tests 0,1,3,4 mis-score every solver whose generate_dna RNG order differs from the reference.

findings.evidence: Test 4 generates from data2 but scans with load_motif_from_df(data); test 5 generates from data3 but scans with load_motif_from_df(data). 'data' is defined only in the test-0/test-3 blocks, not in tests 4/5. Passes in official joint mode (shared namespace) but fails under --isolate with NameError: name 'data' is not defined. Data smell / copy-paste artifact; tests 4/5 likely intended to scan with data2/data3.
findings.suggested_fix: Define 'data' inside test 4 and test 5 (or use data2/data3 as the scan matrix to match the comment intent).

overall_assessment: Not fair to score as-is. 76.1 is a hard blocker: the prompt repeatedly mandates L1 normalization into a 'probability distribution' but the frozen target is L2 (Euclidean) normalized, so any prompt-compliant solver fails (and 76.2, which consumes 76.1's output, fails with it). 76.2 additionally leaves the KL log base unstated (target=natural log; log2 fails). 76.4 is a second blocker for its four position tests: the targets 163/654 are an exact RNG fingerprint of the unscored, under-specified generate_dna (76.3) and are only reproducible by guessing the reference's precise random-call order; its None tests (2/5) are fine. A minor test-case cross-contamination also exists in 76.4 tests 4/5.
